claims.scope: Regression tests preserve the current Surya Siddhanta and Vakya Pancha-Anga and sky-event outputs. No independent published-Panchangam comparison set is registered, so engine-pinned output must not be described as externally verified.

Samvatsara, Ayana, Ritu, lunar-month, Paksha, weekday and Rasi labels combine astronomical calculations with calendar rollover conventions. They require criterion-level locators and regional-scope notes; astronomical correctness alone does not verify the naming convention.

Brahma Muhurta, Abhijit, Amrita Kalam, Rahu Kalam, Gulika, Yamagandam, Varjyam, Durmuhurtham, Bhadra divisions, Sankramana avoidance and Choghadiya are regression-tested formulas from different traditions. No single title-level citation verifies this bundle; each table or formula needs an exact locator and scope crosswalk.

claims.locator: tests/test_eclipses.py
claims.scope: The eclipse event pipeline is regression-tested against Swiss Ephemeris calculations. The ledger does not yet contain an independent event-by-event comparison fixture, so this is engine-pinned rather than externally verified.

Special Yogas, Panchaka labels, Khara month, Pitru Paksha, Simha-Stha, Maudhya, Anandadi Yoga, Disha Shoola, Nakshatra Mukha and Panchaka Rahita are separate traditional classifications. The group exists to expose evidence debt and grants no umbrella textual authority; each component needs its own inspected rule table and regional boundary.

claims.locator: Chapter CIV (104), stanza 4, including its concluding all-planets 11th-house statement
claims.scope: Supports the configured favourable houses counted from Janma Chandra for Surya, Chandra, Mangala, Budha, Guru, Shukra and Shani. The explicit houses in stanza 4 combine with its concluding statement that all Grahas are benefic in the 11th. It does not support the Vedha table, father-son exemptions, Rahu/Ketu convention, named Shani conditions, or the binary reduction of each transit to one verdict.

claims.locator: Phaladeepika, Adhyaya XXVI, slokas 3-8 (printed pp. 287-289); Jataka Parijata, Volume III, Adhyaya XIII, note to sloka 60, printed pp. 833-834 (PDF pp. 127-128)
claims.scope: Supports every configured favourable-house-to-Vedha-house pair for Surya, Chandra, Kuja, Budha, Guru, Shukra and Shani, plus the Surya-Shani and Chandra-Budha exemptions. It does not support this project's Rahu/Ketu policy or named Shani conditions. Brihat Samhita Chapter 104 is not the authority for this layer.

claims.locator: Phaladeepika, Adhyaya XXVI, sloka 2 (printed p. 286), especially the concluding direction that Rahu and Ketu are similar to Surya
claims.scope: The implementation gives Rahu and Ketu Shani's favourable houses (3, 6 and 11) and therefore marks the 10th adverse. Phaladeepika 26.2 directs that both nodes be treated like Surya, whose favourable set is 3, 6, 10 and 11. This directly contradicts the implemented favourable-house set. The passage does not establish whether nodes cause or receive Vedha, so the separate no-Vedha policy remains unverified rather than contradicted by this locator.

claims.locator: Phaladeepika, Adhyaya XXVI, sloka 1 for Janma Chandra as the transit reference and slokas 22-23 (printed pp. 295-296) for Shani's effects in houses 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12
claims.scope: Verifies that these five Shani positions are reckoned from the natal Moon and have adverse classical transit effects. It does not verify grouping houses 12, 1 and 2 under the vernacular name Sade Sati; the names Ashtama Shani and Ardhastama Shani; the rising, peak and setting phase labels; or the deterministic advice sentences. Those remain configured conventional or project-interpreted presentation layers.

The generator verifies the rasi set and every declared graha, house and verdict in transits_cited against computed gochara. The text and advice fields are model interpretation: they are screened for unsupported precision and selected high-stakes directions but are not semantically or scripturally verified. They must never inherit the authority state of their cited transit triples.
Each activity needs rule-level locators; shared defaults must not imply universal textual agreement.

claims.locator: ACTIVITY_RULES['any']; shared scoring pipeline in personal/muhurta.py
claims.scope: The 'Anything auspicious' selector deliberately adds no activity-specific rule. It exposes the finder's shared Panchanga, Choghadiya, Lagna, personal-strength and relative-tier calculations as a source-neutral exploratory ranking. It is not a classical election for an unspecified act, must not be described as scripturally verified, and should yield to every purpose-specific profile when the intended act is known.

claims.locator: Chapter IX, 'Electing a time for marriage,' printed p. 41 (PDF p. 45), especially the Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra and Rasi rules
claims.scope: The inspected passage contradicts the configured wedding Tithi-family scoring. The project penalizes every Jaya Tithi, but Raman names Shukla Tritiya and Trayodashi among the best while rejecting Ashtami. The project rewards every Purna Tithi, which can reward Pournami and Amavasya even though the passage rejects both. Raman also supplies exact weekday, Nakshatra and rising-Rasi lists that the current broad preferences do not represent. This audit claim records evidence debt only and must never be presented as a verified profile.

claims.locator: Full-text scope search of the registered edition found no 'Betrothal,' 'Engagement,' or 'Nischayam' election; nearest candidate is Chapter IX, 'Electing a time for marriage,' printed pp. 41-42 (PDF pp. 45-46)
claims.scope: The configured Engagement profile has no dedicated passage in the inspected Raman edition and must not inherit marriage authority by label similarity. If the neighboring marriage election was intended as its basis, the configured Tithi-family scoring conflicts with it: the project penalizes every Jaya Tithi although Shukla Tritiya and Trayodashi are admitted, and rewards every Purna Tithi although Pournami and Amavasya are rejected. The profile also omits that passage's exact weekday, Nakshatra and rising-Rasi gates. This audit records both the taxonomy gap and the nearest-source conflict; it does not establish a verified Engagement tradition.

claims.locator: Chapter XII, 'House building,' section 'Entering a new house,' printed pp. 52-54 (PDF pp. 56-58)
claims.scope: The current profile is not equivalent to the inspected Gruhapravesha rules. It penalizes the Jaya Tithi family even though Raman explicitly admits Shukla Tritiya and Trayodashi; accepts weekdays outside Raman's Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday list; omits the exact admitted Nakshatra and Tithi gates; and treats fixed Lagna as a preference instead of the stated default rule. The source's Uttarayana, Graha-strength, 8th-house, ritual and advanced-pregnancy checks are not fully automatable and remain practitioner checks. This audit claim records the conflict and must not be presented as verification of the configured scorer.

claims.locator: Chapter XVII, 'Miscellaneous elections,' section 'Filing law-suits,' printed p. 67 (PDF p. 71)
claims.scope: The configured Court profile prefers Mangalavaram, while Raman explicitly directs that Tuesday and Saturday be avoided for filing lawsuits. The project also rewards the entire Jaya Tithi family and penalizes the entire Purna family without support from this passage, and it omits Raman's ten admitted Nakshatras and election-chart requirements. This is a direct weekday contradiction and an incomplete rule profile; the audit claim must not be presented as verification. The separate internal litigation activity has its own audit claim and does not inherit this claim silently.

claims.locator: Chapter XVII, 'Miscellaneous elections,' section 'Filing law-suits,' printed p. 67 (PDF p. 71)
claims.scope: The configured Litigation / contest profile prefers Mangalavaram, while Raman explicitly directs that Tuesday and Saturday be avoided for filing lawsuits. Its Jaya-family reward and Purna-family penalty are not authorized by this passage, and the ten admitted Nakshatras and election-chart requirements are absent. The separate Bhadra Puchha bonus is attributed in code to Muhurta Chintamani and Dharma Sindhu, but those attributions still lack edition-specific verse or page locators and do not cure the weekday contradiction. This audit claim records the conflict and must not be presented as verification.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Pretakriya ka muhurta,' verse 48, printed pp. 47-48 (OCR lines 2956-2971 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Verse 48 and its Hindi commentary forbid cremation during the latter half of Dhanishtha plus Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati: the traditional four-and-a-half Nakshatras. The implementation deliberately marks all of Dhanishtha as Panchaka, so it over-rejects the first half and is not textually exact. The passage also treats Pretakriya after a rite could not be performed at death; it does not authorize ranking Antyeshti as a generic auspicious Choghadiya venture. The profile must remain contradicted until Pada/half-Nakshatra precision and the ritual scope are resolved.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Homahuti Muhurta' and 'Agnivasa,' verses 35-36, printed pp. 43-44 (OCR lines 2773-2796 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Verses 35-36 govern Homa with two computations absent from the profile: a nine-group, three-Nakshatra cycle counted from Surya's Nakshatra that identifies the Graha receiving the offering, and an Agnivasa modulo-four test using the Tithi and weekday. The configured Purna-family reward and Jaya-family penalty conflict with that conditional formula because favorable and unfavorable Agnivasa outcomes occur within both families; Monday/Thursday and fixed-Lagna preferences are not supplied by these verses. The broader label 'Yajna / Homam' also exceeds the cited Homahuti scope. This claim records a direct scoring and taxonomy conflict, not verification of a universal Yajna rule.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, purchase/sale distinction and purchase Muhurta, verse 16, printed pp. 33-34 (OCR lines 2336-2350); marketplace election, verse 17, printed pp. 34-35 (OCR lines 2351-2374)
claims.scope: Verse 16 supports the configured preference for Revati, Shatabhisha, Ashvini, Swati, Shravana and Chitra from the buyer's perspective. Verse 17 supports the disclosed marketplace checks: reject Rikta Tithis, Tuesday and Kumbha Lagna; place Chandra and Shukra in Lagna, keep malefics out of the 8th and 12th, and place benefics in the 2nd, 10th or 11th. The Labh-Choghadiya bonus is a separate project heuristic, not authorized by these verses. Object-specific vehicle, building-land and jewelry profiles remain narrower authorities and take precedence.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Entering the service of a master,' verse 26, printed p. 38 (OCR lines 2565-2577); 'Sandhana Muhurta,' verse 42, printed pp. 45-46 (OCR lines 2880-2891)
claims.scope: The single label combines entering service with contract signing, but the inspected text treats service entry separately and does not equate Sandhana (peace, alliance or friendship) with a modern employment or commercial contract. Verse 26 names seven Nakshatras, four weekdays, benefic occupation of Lagna, Surya or Mangala in the 10th/11th, and employer/employee Yoni and Rasi-lord friendship. The profile implements none of the activity-specific star or relationship criteria and substitutes Amrit Choghadiya, Nanda Tithi and fixed-Lagna preferences unsupported by these passages. This taxonomy and rule mismatch must not be presented as a verified Job or Contract profile.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Dravyaprayoga and taking a loan,' verse 27, printed pp. 38-39 (OCR lines 2578-2599); compare marketplace verse 17, printed pp. 34-35
claims.scope: No inspected passage supplies a universal modern business-launch election. The closest capital-deployment rule, verse 27, names twelve Nakshatras, requires Chara Lagna, benefics in the 5th/9th and an empty 8th; its movable-Lagna requirement directly contradicts the configured Sthira-Lagna bonus. Marketplace transactions and purchase for inventory are separate scopes and cannot silently authorize launch timing. The configured Amrit, Nanda, Wednesday/Thursday and fixed-Lagna profile must not be presented as verified business-launch doctrine.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, 'Shantika and Paushtika Muhurta,' verse 34, printed pp. 42-43 (OCR lines 2749-2772 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Verse 34 governs Shantika and Paushtika rites rather than every ceremony or Puja. It rejects Rikta Tithis, Ashtami, Pournami and Amavasya; this does not match the configured whole-Jaya-family penalty, which catches Ashtami but omits the other cited exclusions and additionally penalizes Tritiya and Trayodashi. The passage also rejects Sunday, Tuesday and Saturday rather than merely rewarding Monday and Thursday. It supplies fifteen Nakshatras and chart placements for Surya, Chandra and Guru that the profile does not implement. Its Sankramana exclusion agrees with the profile, but the inspected passage does not establish the profile's other broad month and Yoga filters. The commentary permits relaxation when an ominous event itself requires emergency Shanti. The generic profile must not be presented as verified from this narrower rite passage.

claims.locator: Nakshatra-prakarana, Dharma-kriya commencement in verse 30, printed pp. 40-41 (OCR lines 2685-2700 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: The nearest inspected commencement rule is specifically for beginning Dharma-kriya, not a universal modern 'new beginning.' Verse 30 names thirteen Nakshatras, Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, Budha or Guru Lagna/varga, Guru in Lagna and the performer's Guru-bala. The profile implements only Wednesday and Thursday as soft bonuses, omits the activity-specific Nakshatra and chart conditions, and substitutes Amrit Choghadiya and Nanda-Tithi rewards not supplied by the passage. The generic taxonomy and unsupported ranking proxies must not be presented as a verified classical election.

claims.locator: Chapter XII, 'House Building' / 'Laying the Foundation,' printed p. 50 (PDF p. 54)
claims.scope: Supports the configured house-foundation lunar-month, Tithi-number, Nakshatra, weekday, solar-Rasi and fixed-Lagna criteria. Full election-chart house occupancy/aspects and ritual site placement are disclosed manual checks. Shared samskara filters, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'Naming the child (Namakarana),' printed p. 21 (PDF p. 25)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Namakarana weekday and Nakshatra admission lists, rejected Tithi numbers, fixed-Lagna preference, timing-after-birth guidance and disclosed election-chart/name checks. Shared samskara filters, Choghadiya and Tithi-family ranking bonuses, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter VII, 'Seemantha,' printed pp. 20-21 (PDF pp. 24-25)
claims.scope: Supports the first-pregnancy and 5th/7th-month boundary; the primary nine-Nakshatra list; rejection of Chaturthi, Shashthi, Ashtami, Navami, Chaturdashi and Amavasya; Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; and rejection of Simha and Vrischika Lagna. The automated profile conservatively omits Pournami because the passage admits it only when Chandra is dignified. Ashwini, Anuradha and Moola are disclosed as unavoidable-circumstance alternatives rather than automated admissions. The empty 8th house, Chandra outside the 8th, relative birth-Nakshatra exclusions and the explicit combustion exception remain manual checks; this unresolved practitioner review caps results below Excellent. Maternal comfort, clinician instructions and medical care always take precedence.

claims.locator: Samskara-prakarana, 'Seemantonnayana Muhurta,' verse 8, printed p. 77 (OCR lines 4157-4180 in the Internet Archive full text)
claims.scope: Verse 8 corroborates the implemented rejection of Rikta Tithis, Amavasya, Dwadashi, Shashthi and Ashtami; its primary and alternative Nakshatra lists together include the profile's nine stars; its alternative weekday rule admits Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; and it likewise reduces the importance of Guru/Shukra combustion. It materially diverges on pregnancy timing by prescribing the 6th or 8th month rather than Raman's 5th or 7th. It also supplies male-planet Lagna/Navamsha and benefic/malefic house-placement rules rather than Raman's ten-Rasi admission set. The product must disclose this lineage choice and must not present one month rule as universal.

claims.locator: Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'First feeding on rice (Annaprasana),' printed pp. 21-22 (PDF pp. 25-26); general Panchanga Suddhi Tithis, Chapter V, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 15)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Annaprasana Nakshatra and weekday admission lists, rejected general-Panchanga-Suddhi Tithis, excluded rising Rasis, age-month guidance and disclosed election-chart checks. Shared samskara filters, Choghadiya and Tithi-family ranking bonuses, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'Ear boring (Karnavedha),' printed p. 22 (PDF p. 26); general Panchanga Suddhi Tithis, Chapter V, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 15)
claims.scope: Supports the daytime-only rule, admitted weekdays, rejected rising Rasis, age guidance, double-Tithi/double-Nakshatra caution, vacant-8th requirement and general-Panchanga-Suddhi Tithi exclusions. Age, transition-count and election-house checks remain manual. Shared samskara filters, Tithi-family ranking, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'Tonsure (Chowlam),' printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 26-27)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Shukla-Paksha, forenoon, combustion, Tithi, weekday, Nakshatra and conservative rising-Rasi rules plus disclosed age, pregnancy, solar-season and election-chart checks. Shared samskara filters, Tithi-family ranking, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'Commencing education (Aksharabhyasa),' printed p. 23 (PDF p. 27)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Vidyarambha weekday, Nakshatra and movable-or-common rising-Rasi admission lists plus disclosed age, forenoon/noon and election-chart guidance. Shared samskara filters, Choghadiya and Tithi-family ranking, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter VIII, 'Post-natal ceremonies' / 'Investiture of sacred thread (Upanayanam),' printed pp. 23-24 (PDF pp. 27-28)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Upanayana lunar months, Uttarayana solar Rasis, exact Paksha-qualified Tithis, weekdays, Nakshatras, admitted rising Rasis and before-noon rule plus disclosed age, conditional Budha combustion and election-chart checks. Shared samskara filters, Tithi-family ranking, personal scoring and relative tiers require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter IV, 'Influence of Nakshatras,' movable-Nakshatra classification, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 14)
claims.scope: Supports only the configured +1 preference for five movable Nakshatras when acquiring vehicles; the passage does not reject every other Nakshatra. The Labh-Choghadiya, Bhadra-Tithi, Friday and fixed-Lagna ranking preferences are disclosed project rules and do not inherit authority from this citation.

claims.locator: Chapter XII, 'Digging Wells,' printed p. 51 (PDF p. 55)
claims.scope: Supports the configured well-digging Nakshatra and rising-Rasi admission lists plus the disclosed Surya-in-Lagna hard-rock caution. Shukra/Chandra Kendra placement and the abundant-sweet-water condition remain manual chart checks. Shared ranking and personal factors require separate authority.

claims.locator: Chapter XII, 'Laying the Foundation,' roofing-stage instruction, printed p. 50 (PDF p. 54)
claims.scope: Supports only the configured Vrishabha-or-Tula rising-Rasi admission rule for roofing. The passage distinguishes roofing from foundation laying but supplies no separate weekday, Tithi or Nakshatra list for this stage. The Panchaka-Nakshatra restriction is a separately implemented project rule and does not inherit authority from this citation.

claims.locator: Chapter XVI, 'Electing Head of the State' and 'Coronation,' printed p. 66 (PDF p. 70)
claims.scope: The coronation paragraph explicitly applies the immediately preceding head-of-state rules. This supports the configured Nakshatra, exact Tithi and admitted rising-Rasi lists plus the disclosed election-chart checks and the traditional-coronation and democratic-government alternatives. Shared samskara exclusions and the Urdhva-Mukha preference are separately implemented project rules and do not inherit authority from this citation.

claims.locator: Chapter XIII, 'Felling Trees,' printed p. 58 (PDF p. 62)
claims.scope: Supports felling trees during Chandra's last quarter, represented by Krishna Ashtami through Amavasya, and the disclosed dry-Rasi/dry-Graha chart check. The Panchaka-Nakshatra restriction is a separately implemented project rule and does not inherit authority from this citation.

claims.locator: Chapter XV, 'Surgical Operations,' printed pp. 64-65 (PDF pp. 68-69)
claims.scope: Supports the configured Tuesday-or-Saturday, waxing Chaturthi/Navami/Chaturdashi and Ardra/Jyeshtha/Ashlesha/Moola admission rules plus the disclosed natal-Chandra, operated-body-part, Mangala, 8th-house, relevant-house and Mangala-Shani chart checks. The Vishti-Karana rejection is a separately implemented project rule and does not inherit authority from this citation. Medical urgency and clinician instructions always override electional timing.

claims.locator: Chapter X, 'Buying Jewelry,' printed p. 45 (PDF p. 49)
claims.scope: Supports only the disclosed requirement that Surya and Chandra be well situated and aspected, plus the passage's general instruction to avoid unfavorable Tithis and Nakshatras. It does not supply a jewelry-specific weekday, Tithi, Nakshatra, Lagna or Choghadiya list. The configured Labh-Choghadiya, Bhadra-Tithi, Friday/Thursday and fixed-Lagna preferences are disclosed project heuristics and do not inherit authority from this citation.

claims.locator: Chapter XIV, 'Journeys' and 'Pilgrimage,' printed pp. 60-62 (PDF pp. 64-66)
claims.scope: The pilgrimage paragraph explicitly incorporates the earlier journey rules. This supports rejecting Chaturdashi and Full/New Chandra days, preferring the ten named journey Nakshatras, rejecting Guru combustion and disclosing Guru-in-Lagna-or-9th as a chart check. The Vishti-Karana rejection follows the separately cited general Panchanga-Suddhi rule. The configured Chara-Lagna preference is a project heuristic and does not inherit authority from this citation; Raman instead names six individual favorable journey Rasis.

claims.locator: Chapter XIV, 'Journeys' and 'Long-distance Journeys,' printed pp. 60-61 (PDF pp. 64-65)
claims.scope: Supports configured hard rejection of Bharani/Krittika, preference for the ten named journey Nakshatras, and the disclosed Lagna, Guru/Shukra, waxing-Chandra, Mangala and 7th-house chart checks. Vishti rejection follows the separately cited general Panchanga-Suddhi rule. Chara-Lagna and Tiryan-Mukha bonuses are separately attributed project rules. Two source corrections remain outside the configured claim because existing tests pin contrary behavior: Chaturdashi/Full/New Chandra rejection, and time-of-day exceptions to Disha Shoola. Both require explicit owner approval.

claims.locator: Chapter XII, 'Buying Lands for Buildings,' printed p. 53 (PDF p. 57)
claims.scope: Supports the configured building-land purchase weekday and Nakshatra admission lists, hard Rikta-Tithi rejection and fixed-Lagna preference. Weekday-lord, Guru, Mangala and house-lord placement conditions remain manual checks. It does not support elections for purchasing a completed house, which Raman treats separately.
